result.summary: Partly done: the decay-rate check and the 3.55 keV line status are complete, but the table of X-ray limits versus mass is not. (1) Decay-rate check (f-005; tc-...-25, tc-...-27): the server's rate matches Gamma = 1.38e-32 s^-1 (sin^2 2theta/1e-10)(m_s/keV)^5 to within about 1.5%. At m_s = 7.1 keV and sin^2 2theta = 1e-10 the tool gives 2.46e-28 s^-1 (formula 2.49e-28), with E = 3.55 keV and lifetime 4.07e27 s. At 20 keV and 1e-12 it gives 4.36e-28 s^-1 (formula 4.42e-28), with E = 10 keV. The rate normalisation in arXiv:2405.17861 Eq. 2 (1.36e-32 s^-1 at sin^2 2theta = 1e-10 and 1 keV) falls in the same range. Whole-halo fluxes at 7.1 keV and 1e-10 are 4.68 ph/s/cm^2 for the Milky Way centre, 6.89e-4 for M31 and 3.55e-5 for Perseus (f_DM = 1, no field-of-view cut). The tool's built-in NuSTAR M31 (Roach+2020) and XMM blank-sky (Dessert+2020) limits exclude both test points. (2) DW benchmark grid at 4 masses x 3 mixings (f-006; CSV /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sterile-bbn-xray/runs/261021_110150/sterile_nu_grid_DW_5199ae.csv): no point is BBN-excluded (Delta N_eff <= 2.9e-3). Omega_s h^2 is 0.087 at 10 keV and 1e-10, 0.30 at 20 keV and 1e-10 (overcloses), and 1.58 at 50 keV and 1e-10 (overcloses). At mixings of 1e-12 to 1e-14, Omega_s h^2 <= 0.016, so a non-DW mechanism is needed. Only the 1e-10 mixing was run through the X-ray tool at 7.1 keV, and only 1e-12 at 20 keV. (3) Status of the 3.55 keV line (f-012, cited in references.bib under key arxiv251024560): XRISM Resolve stacked ten clusters for 3.75 Ms (arXiv:2510.24560) and found no unidentified lines. Its 3-sigma limit is Gamma ~ 1.0e-27 s^-1 at m_s ~ 7.1 keV, 3-4 times stronger than Hitomi but still 5 times above the Bulbul+2014 XMM signal, so the line is constrained but not ruled out. Scaling the tool's rate turns this into sin^2 2theta < ~4e-10. (4) NuSTAR 11-year stray-light limits (arXiv:2405.17861, Fig. 3, 95% CL, m_s ~ 6-40 keV; f-013) reach the lower edge of resonant-production predictions, but the numbers at 7, 10 and 20 keV were not read off the figure. Open items: the table of sin^2 2theta limits at 7, 10, 20 and 50 keV has no figure-read values yet (q-08). Searches for 2024-2026 eROSITA and INTEGRAL/SPI limits found nothing (dead end x-01). The XRISM-derived limit at 7.1 keV is the only quoted entry; 10, 20 and 50 keV need Fig. 3 of 2405.17861 and an SPI or NuSTAR GC source. The NuSTAR paper was not added to the bib.

result.summary: All four arXiv IDs resolve to real papers (f-001): 2507.18752 (Vogel et al. 2025), 2502.17374 (Gorbunov, Kalashnikov and Krugan 2025), 2601.03346 (Cline and Xu 2026) and 2609.31340 (Gorbunov and Kalashnikov 2026). So 2609.31340 is genuine and q-03 is answered. I read the full text of 2507.18752, cited it in runs/261021_110150/references.bib and saved the text as runs/261021_110150/2507.18752.txt (f-002). The paper's viable region is m_s >~ 10 keV and sin^2(2theta) <~ 1e-14 for L >~ 0.5 at T > 20 MeV. Its bounds: NuSTAR sin^2(2theta) <~ 1e-12 at 6-40 keV, INTEGRAL/SPI <~ 3e-14 above 40 keV, m_th > 8.4 keV from galaxy counts, m_th > 8.5 keV from counts plus lensing, and a Lyman-alpha preference m_th = 4.1 (+33.3/-1.5) keV. Tool tests (f-003; CSVs sterile_nu_grid_SF_fdf543.csv and sterile_nu_grid_SF_d81486.csv) at m_s = 10, 20 and 30 keV with sin^2(2theta) = 1e-14 in SF mode give Delta N_eff ~ 1e-8 and BBN Delta chi^2 = 0 (allowed). At 20 keV Yp = 0.24682 and D/H = 2.4433e-5. Omega_s h^2 is 0.122, 0.490 and 1.10 at L = 1e-3 and ten times larger at L = 0.1; all of these points are flagged as overclosing. The tool cannot test the paper's claims. Its L is capped at 0.1 while the paper needs L >~ 0.5. Its SF Delta N_eff is a heuristic (0.1 x the DW value). It does not feed a xi_e effect into Yp, so the |xi_e| <~ 0.03 condition cannot be checked. Its SF Omega_s h^2 is not a Boltzmann calculation, so the overclosure flag does not contradict the paper. The BBN 'allowed' verdict is trivially true rather than supporting evidence. The server uses Yp = 0.2449 +/- 0.004 and D/H = 2.547 +/- 0.025 (relevant to q-02). Mechanism map (f-004) from the 2502.17374, 2609.31340 and 2601.03346 abstracts only: flavor-dependent asymmetries reopen lighter masses and smaller mixings; large L saturates resonant production, leaving about a two-decade window in sin^2(2theta); inflaton-decay reheating production with BR <~ 1e-4 populates cold DM below the X-ray limits. The survey criteria are only partly met. The full text of 2502.17374 was not read, so its viable ranges have no verbatim quotes. The 2024+ structure-formation search found only arXiv:2409.18917 (mixed WDM from Milky Way satellites), which was neither read nor cited. Open question q-07 asks for a BBN code that accepts xi_e, which a real test would need.

result.summary:
All three contested findings now have verbatim quotes. The X-ray limit table covers five masses, but only one value is read directly from a primary source; the rest come from a secondary summary. Viability table: f-018. Findings f-014 to f-018 and dead end x-02 are posted.

(1) f-002, re-supported by f-014, quoting the 2507.18752 full text (runs/261021_110150/2507.18752.txt, tc-...-w2-d-05-72). Viable region: 'L≳0.5 ... m_s≳10 keV and sin^2(2θ)≲10^-14'. NuSTAR: 'sin^2(2θ)≲10^-12 in the 6–40 keV mass range'. INTEGRAL/SPI: 'exclude lifetimes below ∼10^20 s at 95% CL [corresponding to sin^2(2θ)≲3×10^-14] in the ≳40 keV mass regime'. Structure formation: m_th > 8.4 keV from galaxy counts, m_th > 8.5 keV from counts plus strong lensing, and a Lyman-alpha preference of m_th = 4.1 (+33.3/-1.5) keV.

(2) f-012, re-supported by f-015, quoting the 2510.24560 abstract (tc-...-84). XRISM stacked 3.75 Ms of data on ten clusters over 2.5-15 keV. Its 3-sigma limit is Γ ∼ 1.0e-27 s^-1 at m_s ∼ 7.1 keV, which converts to sin^2 2θ < ~4e-10 (my conversion, not a quote).

(3) f-013, partly re-supported and downgraded to medium by f-016 (tc-...-77, -80, -85). Eq. 2 of 2405.17861 reads 1.36×10^-22 (m_s/keV)^5 sin^2 2θ s^-1. That exponent is correct as written, because sin^2 2θ is not normalised there; it equals 1.36e-32 s^-1 at sin^2 2θ = 1e-10. The paper gives 95% limits for m_s = 6-40 keV, with observed limits stronger than expected at 8-9 and 23-25 keV and an instrumental excess at 40 keV. Fig. 3 is missing from the HTML rendering. The Fig. 1 image was downloaded (Figure 15, figures_2405.17861/fig01.png) but not read numerically. So the 7, 10 and 20 keV entries rest on the secondary summary value of <~1e-12. 2405.17861 is now cited in references.bib under arxiv240517861 (tc-...-96).

(4) X-ray limit table (f-017), cross-checked with the server's line tool:
- 7.1 keV: XRISM < ~4e-10 (3 sigma); NuSTAR <~1e-12.
- 10 keV: NuSTAR <~1e-12. At 1e-12 the tool gives Γ = 1.36e-29 s^-1, E = 5 keV and lifetime 7.35e28 s, not excluded by its tables (tc-...-95).
- 20 keV: NuSTAR <~1e-12. The tool's own tables exclude 1e-12 (d-02).
- 40 keV: the upper edge of NuSTAR coverage, where SPI <~3e-14 takes over.
- 50 keV: SPI <~3e-14. At 3e-14 the tool gives Γ = 1.28e-27 s^-1 and lifetime 7.8e26 s, not excluded (tc-...-94).
Warning: the SPI quote equates a lifetime of ~1e20 s with a mixing of 3e-14, but the tool gives 7.8e26 s at that mixing, a gap of about 7 orders of magnitude. The SPI mixing value needs checking against the primary SPI paper. My search for a 2024-2026 SPI or NuSTAR limit above 40 keV found nothing (dead end x-02, tc-...-86).

(5) Viability table (f-018):
- Dodelson-Widrow: excluded as all of the dark matter. Its dark-matter line (2.55e-10 at 7.1 keV, 1.37e-10 at 10 keV, 3.9e-11 at 20 keV, 7.6e-12 at 50 keV; server normalisation from f-008) lies above the NuSTAR and SPI limits, so X-ray is the binding constraint and BBN is not. Correction to the wording in f-018: at 7.1 keV the dark-matter line (2.55e-10) sits below the XRISM limit (~4e-10), so XRISM alone does not exclude it there; NuSTAR does.
- Shi-Fuller with L >~ 0.5 at T > 20 MeV: viable at m_s >~ 10 keV and sin^2 2θ <~ 1e-14. The binding constraints are X-ray and m_th. Provenance is the 2507.18752 quotes; the server cannot test this because it caps L at 0.1.
- Flavor-dependent asymmetry (2502.17374) and saturation at large L (2609.31340): lighter masses at smaller mixing, and about a two-decade window in mixing. Abstract only.
- Reheating production (2601.03346, branching ratio <~ 1e-4): cold dark matter below the X-ray limits. Abstract only.

result.summary: Normalization (f-019): the published DW fit in arXiv:1705.01837 (Abazajian review) Eq. 37 is m_s ~ 3.40 keV (sin^2 2theta/1e-8)^-0.615 (Omega_DM/0.26)^0.5 x 0.527 erfc[-1.15 (T_QCD/170 MeV)^2.15]. It is cited in references.bib under key arxiv170501837. I inverted it by hand. Its dark-matter line sits at sin^2 2theta ~ 1.23e-8 (3 keV), 3.0e-9 (7.1 keV), 1.73e-9 (10 keV), 5.6e-10 (20 keV) and 1.26e-10 (50 keV). The QCD-era uncertainty (T_QCD 150-200 MeV) moves these by about +10%/-7%. The server line from predict_sterile_nu_grid (sterile_nu_grid_DW_2461e9.csv, Omega h^2 = 0.119-0.120) is 1.2e-9, 2.55e-10, 1.37e-10, 3.9e-11 and 7.6e-12. The published normalization therefore needs 10-17x more mixing than the server and 3.4-5.5x more than the brief's formula, and it scales differently with mass and mixing. Verdict at 7.1 keV (f-020): against the XRISM limit of about 4e-10, the server line (2.55e-10) survives, while the brief's line (7.65e-10) and the published line (3.0e-9) are excluded. Using the published normalization, DW at 7.1 keV is excluded by about 7.5x. m_th (f-021): I used the DW-to-thermal mapping m_s = 4.43 keV (m_th)^(4/3) from Viel+2005 (astro-ph/0501562). I downloaded that paper but did not quote the coefficient verbatim from it. This gives m_th = 0.75, 1.42, 1.84, 3.10 and 6.16 keV at m_s = 3, 7.1, 10, 20 and 50 keV. Lyman-alpha (m_th > 4-6 keV) then needs m_s > 28-48 keV, and satellite counts (m_th > 8.4 keV) need m_s > 76 keV. At those masses the DW line under any of the three normalizations sits well above the NuSTAR (~1e-12) and SPI (~3e-14) ceilings, so the surviving DW mass interval is empty. BBN (f-022): these are analytic results from linearized f-009 slopes, not server runs. Upper bounds on Delta N_eff at 95%, relative to the SM: with the brief's data, 0.32 from Yp only, 0.58 from D/H only and 0.47 combined. With the server's data, 0.46, 0.66 and 0.61. The server tool itself quotes 0.548. The SM D/H sits 2.9-4.1 sigma low, so D/H prefers Delta N_eff ~ 0.3 and the bound moves by 0.1-0.2 depending on the baseline. For the joint bound I used dYp/dxi_e = -0.25 and 2-dof Delta chi^2 < 5.99. Brief data: Delta N_eff in [0.04, 0.48], with xi_e = 0.0073 + 0.054 Delta N_eff +/- 0.029. Server data: Delta N_eff in [0.13, 0.50], with xi_e = 0.0077 + 0.054 Delta N_eff +/- 0.039. Overall |xi_e| <~ 0.03-0.06. Question q-09 is posted. Open items: the Viel coefficient and the full Eq. 37 citation still need verbatim quotes, and dD/H/dxi_e was neglected.

findings.claim: Mechanism map (from literature quotes, not computed by tools). Shi-Fuller resonant production with L >~ 0.5 above 20 MeV is viable at m_s >~ 10 keV and sin^2(2theta) <~ 1e-14 (2507.18752). Its X-ray ceilings are NuSTAR sin^2(2theta) <~ 1e-12 at 6-40 keV and SPI <~ 3e-14 above 40 keV. Its structure-formation bounds are m_th > 8.4-8.5 keV (galaxy counts and lensing) or the Lyman-alpha preference m_th ~ 4.1 keV. Flavor-dependent asymmetries, which work best with inverted ordering, open lower mixing angles and give colder spectra that reopen lighter m_s (2502.17374, abstract only). Large L saturates resonant production, which leaves about a two-decade window in sin^2(2theta) (2609.31340, abstract only). Inflaton-decay reheating production with BR <~ 1e-4 gives cold DM at mixings below the X-ray limits, which oscillation production cannot populate (2601.03346, abstract only).

findings.claim: XRISM Resolve stacked 3.75 Ms of data on ten galaxy clusters (arXiv:2510.24560, 2025) and found no unidentified lines over 2.5-15 keV. Its 3-sigma upper limit on the decay rate of an m_s ~ 7.1 keV particle (E = 3.55 keV) is Gamma ~ 1.0e-27 s^-1. Final viability table in the (m_s, sin^2 2θ) plane:
- DW (non-resonant): not viable as all of the dark matter. The DM line sits at sin^2 2θ = 2.55e-10 (7.1 keV), 1.37e-10 (10 keV), 3.9e-11 (20 keV) and 7.6e-12 (50 keV) (server normalization, f-008). All of these lie above the XRISM limit (~4e-10 at 7.1 keV is the only point below the line's value there, but it sits within a factor of 1.6) and above the NuSTAR <~1e-12 and SPI <~3e-14 limits. Binding constraint: X-ray. BBN is not binding; Delta chi^2 < 0.15 along the line. Provenance: f-008 and f-014 to f-017. 2507.18752 states "the original DW mechanism is ruled out as producing the entirety of the dark matter".
- Shi-Fuller with L >~ 0.5 at T > 20 MeV: viable at m_s >~ 10 keV and sin^2 2θ <~ 1e-14. Binding constraints are X-ray (NuSTAR 1e-12, SPI 3e-14 above 40 keV) and structure formation (m_th > 8.4-8.5 keV from galaxy counts and lensing, against a Lyman-alpha preference of 4.1 keV). Provenance: verbatim quotes from 2507.18752 (f-014). Server BBN is trivially allowed (f-003), but this is not an independent test because the tool caps L at 0.1.
- Flavor-dependent asymmetry (2502.17374): lighter m_s at smaller mixing, with BBN limits weakened and colder spectra. Abstract only; no numerical ranges are quoted. Saturation at large L (2609.31340) leaves a window of about two decades in sin^2 2θ; abstract only.
- Reheating (inflaton decay, BR <~ 1e-4; 2601.03346): cold DM at mixings below the X-ray limits. Binding constraint: X-ray only. Abstract only.

The published DW normalization (Abazajian 2017 review, arXiv:1705.01837 Eq. 37, a fit from Ref. [120]) is m_s ~ 3.40 keV (sin^2 2theta/1e-8)^-0.615 (Omega_DM/0.26)^0.5 x 0.527 erfc[-1.15 (T_QCD/170 MeV)^2.15]. Inverting it gives a DM line at sin^2 2theta ~ 1.23e-8 (3 keV), 3.0e-9 (7.1 keV), 1.73e-9 (10 keV), 5.6e-10 (20 keV) and 1.26e-10 (50 keV). The server line from the tool is 1.2e-9, 2.55e-10, 1.37e-10, 3.9e-11 and 7.6e-12 (Omega_s h^2 = 0.119-0.120). So the published line needs 10x (3 keV) to 17x (50 keV) more mixing than the server and 3.4-5.5x more than the brief's formula. The two differ in shape as well as normalization: Omega is proportional to m^2 (sin^2 2theta)^1.23 rather than m^1.8 times sin^2 2theta.

evidence.note: I inverted the formula by hand at T_QCD = 170 MeV, where the erfc factor is 0.999. Omega_DM = 0.26 corresponds to Omega h^2 ~ 0.12 for h = 0.68. Varying T_QCD over 150-200 MeV changes the erfc factor from 0.94 to 1.04, which moves the required mixing by about +10% / -7%. This is the QCD-era uncertainty of the formula. It is much smaller than the factor 10-17 gap to the server.

findings.claim: At 7.1 keV the DW verdict depends on the normalization when compared with the XRISM limit sin^2 2theta < ~4e-10 (f-012). The server line (2.55e-10) survives XRISM. The brief's line (7.65e-10) and the published Abazajian line (3.0e-9, about +10%/-7% from T_QCD) are excluded, the published one by about 7.5x. Since the published normalization is the reference calculation, DW dark matter at 7.1 keV is excluded by XRISM alone. The server's DW Omega_s h^2 underestimates the mixing needed by about 12x at 7.1 keV, so server-based DW statements are not conservative.

On the DW DM line, the standard DW-to-thermal mapping m_s = 4.43 keV (m_th/keV)^(4/3) (Viel et al. 2005, astro-ph/0501562; text downloaded, but the formula was not quoted verbatim from it) gives m_th = 0.75 keV (m_s = 3 keV), 1.42 keV (7.1 keV), 1.84 keV (10 keV), 3.10 keV (20 keV) and 6.16 keV (50 keV). Lyman-alpha m_th > 4 (6) keV requires m_s > 28 (48) keV, and satellite counts m_th > 8.4 keV require m_s > 76 keV. At m_s >= 28 keV the DW line has sin^2 2theta ~ 3e-10 (published normalization) or about 1e-11 (server). Both values lie far above the NuSTAR ceiling of about 1e-12 at 6-40 keV and the SPI ceiling of about 3e-14 above 40 keV (f-002). The surviving DW mass interval is therefore empty under all three normalizations.

evidence.note: The 4.43 keV (m_th)^(4/3) coefficient is the commonly used Viel+2005 value. I did not read or quote it verbatim from the downloaded text, so someone should confirm it there. The 50 keV DW point under the server normalization (7.6e-12) is above the SPI limit of 3e-14 by more than 100x.

findings.claim: BBN robustness check. I used linearized f-009 slopes (dYp/dN_eff = 0.0135, dD/H/dN_eff = 0.331e-5) about the server SM values (Yp = 0.246815, D/H = 2.4433e-5). The 95% upper bounds on Delta N_eff are given as Delta chi^2 = 3.84 against the SM, with Delta chi^2 = 3.84 against the best fit in brackets. Brief data (Yp 0.245 +/- 0.003, D/H 2.53 +/- 0.03): Yp-only 0.32; D/H-only 0.58 [0.44]; combined 0.47 [0.37]. Server data (Yp 0.2449 +/- 0.004, D/H 2.547 +/- 0.025): Yp-only 0.46; D/H-only 0.66 [0.46]; combined 0.61 [0.43]. The server tool reports 0.548. D/H alone prefers Delta N_eff = 0.26 (brief data) or 0.31 (server data) because the SM D/H sits 2.9 or 4.1 sigma low, so the bound depends on the baseline at the 0.1-0.2 level. Joint bound with dYp/dxi_e = -0.25, assuming D/H does not depend on xi_e, using 2-dof Delta chi^2 = 5.99. Brief data: Delta N_eff in [0.04, 0.48] and xi_e = 0.0073 + 0.054 Delta N_eff +/- 0.029. Server data: Delta N_eff in [0.13, 0.50] and xi_e = 0.0077 + 0.054 Delta N_eff +/- 0.039. So |xi_e| <~ 0.03-0.06 overall, and a positive xi_e of about 0.03 compensates Delta N_eff of about 0.5 in Yp.

evidence.note: These are analytic Gaussian calculations, not server runs. My linearized combined server-data bound (0.61) differs from the tool's 0.548, probably because the fit is nonlinear or the tool uses a different chi^2 convention. I neglected the D/H dependence on xi_e (dD/H/dxi_e).

questions.text: Does the sterile-nu server model resonant (Shi-Fuller) production with a lepton asymmetry, or only non-resonant production? Its answer bounds how much of the viable-region claim can be computed rather than quoted.
Which BBN observational values does the server use (Yp, D/H), and do they match Yp = 0.245 +/- 0.003 and D/H = (2.53 +/- 0.03)e-5?
Is arXiv:2609.31340 a real paper? The ID format suggests a possible error.
Is there a citable arXiv source for the eROSITA eFEDS line limits, given that the web snippet is not quotable?
What is the current status of the 3.55 keV line after XRISM?
Facility dispatch is not needed unless the d-01 grids exceed what runs locally in minutes. The 400-point grids should run locally.

A real Shi-Fuller BBN test needs Yp computed with a nu_e degeneracy xi_e(T~1 MeV) taken from the L-evolution in 2507.18752. That requires a BBN code that accepts xi_e, such as PRIMAT, AlterBBN or PRyMordial with xi. Is such a code available to the team?

What are the numerical sin^2 2theta upper limits at m_s = 7, 10, 20 keV in Fig. 3 of arXiv:2405.17861 (NuSTAR stray light), and at 50 keV from INTEGRAL/SPI or NuSTAR GC? Answering this needs get_paper_figures or a deeper read of the text.

Should the sterile-nu server's DW relic formula (Omega ~ 0.1 (s/1e-9)(m/3 keV)^1.8) be replaced with the Abazajian 2006/2017 fit, which requires 10-17x more mixing on the DM line, and is the server's SM D/H = 2.443e-5 (2.9-4.1 sigma below the data) a nuclear-rate choice that biases its Delta N_eff bounds?
What Yp/D/H/N_eff baselines to quote (brief's Yp=0.245/D/H=2.5e-5 vs server's Yp=0.2449/D/H=2.547e-5/Planck N_eff=2.99+/-0.17) and how does Delta N_eff<0.5-0.6 bound shift between them?
What is the DW normalization discrepancy (server vs brief vs Abazajian 1705.01837 Eq.37) and which to adopt for the Omega_s h^2=0.12 line when assessing X-ray exclusion?
Do 2024-2026 XRISM/NuSTAR/SPI limits fully close the DW DM line, and what windows remain for SF resonant (L>0.5) and reheating (BR~1e-4) production at m_s>10 keV and sin^2 2theta<1e-14?

What is the primary INTEGRAL/SPI paper definition that makes its sin^2 2theta<3e-14 at >40 keV correspond to tau~1e20 s vs tool tau 7.8e26 s at same mixing - is it f_DM, profile, or sin^2 2theta normalization?
Does the Viel+2005 coefficient 4.43 keV*(m_th/1keV)^{4/3} assume a specific transfer-function definition (half-mode vs free-streaming) that shifts the m_s>28-48 keV Lyman-alpha requirement?
Can the server's SF L=0.1 cap be circumvented with an analytic xi_e correction to Yp (dYp/dxi_e~-0.25) to test the L>0.5 claim's BBN consistency without a full Boltzmann run?

issues.text: For keV-scale DM at sin^2 2theta below about 1e-8, the extra radiation from non-resonant production is negligible (Delta N_eff << 0.1). Yp and D/H shifts will then be indistinguishable from SBBN, and the BBN constraint is effectively vacuous in the region of interest. The direction must establish this from the tool output and say so explicitly. Without lepton asymmetry, BBN bites only at large mixing or low mass. Do not present a trivial BBN pass as a non-trivial constraint.

Set the scan ranges after describe_sterile_nu_tools reports the validity range, not before. Also run one zero-mixing (SBBN) baseline point, so that Yp and D/H deviations are reported both against the code's own SBBN value and against observation. This separates a code offset from a sterile-neutrino effect.

Budget risk: scan, plot, grid, bbn_impact, SBL check, DW checks and skill loading together approach 15 calls. Drop or defer check_sterile_nu_sbl_anomaly. The eV-scale SBL point is not keV dark matter and is tangential to the task. Merge the DW-scaling checks into the predict_sterile_nu_grid call.

The DW scaling formula is approximate, and published coefficients vary by factors of about 2. The pass criterion should be agreement within a factor of about 2, with the tool's exact normalization stated. It should not be treated as a precision test.

The benchmark mixings 1e-12 and 1e-14 at 7.1 keV are uninformative. The 3.55 keV line corresponds to sin^2 2theta of about (2-7)e-11. Add that point and drop the low-mixing points at 7.1 keV to save calls. Choose mixings near the expected limit at each mass, which falls steeply as m_s^-5.

The eROSITA claim comes only from a non-citable web snippet. It may enter the table only if an arXiv paper is found and quoted; otherwise mark it 'unverified'. Limits quoted from different papers assume different DM profiles and J-factors, so record the assumed profile for each table entry. Without it, comparisons across experiments are not like-for-like.
Budget: 4 xray-line calls, 4 or more searches, downloads, chunk reads, figures and cites can exceed 15 calls. Cap the searches at 3, the full texts at 2, and get_paper_figures at 1.

arXiv:2609.31340 refers to September 2026 and may not exist yet, which makes it a likely hallucinated ID. It must not be cited unless get_arxiv_metadata resolves it. Also verify 2601.03346; the brief notes that both were seen only as snippets.

If the server models only non-resonant production with no lepton-asymmetry input, predict_sterile_nu at sin^2 2theta = 1e-14 will return a negligible Omega h^2. That result says nothing about the Shi-Fuller claims. Check the tool's input schema for a xi or L parameter before spending calls. If none exists, replace the tool tests with a literature cross-check of the BBN xi_e bounds (for example 2005.06721, quoted). Do not report any tool-computed dYp/dxi_e.

The mapping from Lyman-alpha m_th to m_s depends on the production mechanism: DW, resonant, and reheating or decay mechanisms all map differently. Quote the mapping each paper uses rather than applying a single conversion. Also include the phase-space (Tremaine-Gunn) lower bound on m_s from a cited source.

contested.reason: The quoted evidence is a download confirmation (tc-...-30) and characters 0-9000 of the paper (tc-...-37), which show only the title, authors and affiliations. None of the claimed numbers appear in the quoted excerpts: L >~ 0.5, m_s >~ 10 keV, sin^2 2theta <~ 1e-14, m_th > 8.4/8.5 keV, m_th = 4.1 (+33.3/-1.5) keV, NuSTAR 1e-12, SPI 3e-14. They may appear later in the 62k-character file, but the cited excerpts do not contain them.

The 2507.18752 numbers depend on the unevidenced f-002. Several specifics are not in the truncated abstracts quoted: the inverted-ordering preference and 'colder spectra' for 2502.17374, and the 'about two-decade window in sin^2 2theta' for 2609.31340. tc-...-51 is a pre-2024 review listing and supports none of these details.

tc-...-61 is an affiliations chunk (characters 9000-14000) and tc-...-62 is only a citation confirmation. Neither contains the 3.75 Ms exposure, the 2.5-15 keV band, Gamma ~ 1.0e-27 s^-1, the comparison with Hitomi or the comparison with Bulbul+2014. Only the final scaling (1e-27 / 2.46e-28 = 4.1, giving about 4e-10) can be checked, and it is correct given those inputs.

The excerpts (title page and methods text on CXB fitting) do not contain Eq. 2, the Fig. 3 axis range or the 'bottom edge of theoretical predictions' quote. The claim also has an arithmetic inconsistency. The server's rate implies a coefficient of 2.46e-28 / (7.1^5 x 1e-10) = 1.36e-32, so the paper's 1.36e-32 matches the server to within about 0.3% rather than sitting 1% above it. The quoted '1.36e-22' also mis-transcribes the exponent.

issues.text: The DW normalization ambiguity decides the DW verdict at 7.1 keV. The server's DM line is at 2.55e-10. The brief's formula gives about 7.6e-10. The XRISM-only limit is about 4e-10. So DW at 3.5 keV is allowed under one normalization and excluded under the other. Neither normalization has been checked against a published DW production calculation, including its QCD-era uncertainty.

The SM D/H baseline (2.4433e-5) is 2.9 sigma below the brief's value and about 4 sigma below the server's 2.547 +/- 0.025. Because exclusion uses Delta chi^2 relative to the SM, extra radiation partly improves the D/H fit. This is why 1 keV at 3e-7 (Yp at +2.3 sigma) has Delta chi^2 of only 0.44. The Delta N_eff < 0.548 bound is therefore sensitive to the nuclear-rate choice and the baseline. This does not change the DW conclusion, but it matters for resonant-production claims.

The core deliverable, sin^2 2theta limits as a function of m_s, is missing at 10, 20 and 50 keV. NuSTAR Fig. 3 values were not read. No INTEGRAL/SPI or eROSITA 2024-2026 limit was sourced. The only number entering the viability table relies on the unevidenced f-002, so the viable region cannot yet be stated quantitatively from verified sources.

SF mode cannot reach L >~ 0.5, does not feed xi_e into BBN, and uses a heuristic Delta N_eff. As a result, no tool-computed BBN check of the resonant-production viability claims exists. The dYp/dxi_e ~ -0.25 check from the brief has not been done.

No thermal-equivalent m_th was computed for any point, so Lyman-alpha and satellite bounds were not applied to the DW line. As a result, the claim that 'DW is excluded by X-ray plus structure formation' was not quantified.

contested.reason: The tool values at 10 keV (Gamma 1.36e-29 s^-1, lifetime 7.35e28 s) and 50 keV (1.28e-27 s^-1, 7.84e26 s) match the excerpts. Two parts do not hold. (1) The 'not excluded' and 'excluded' verdicts at 10, 20 and 50 keV cannot be seen in the truncated excerpts. (2) The claimed 7-order inconsistency in the SPI quote is almost certainly a seconds-versus-years slip. The tool's own output at 50 keV and 3e-14 is 2.48e19 yr. Read as ~1e20 yr (3.2e27 s), the SPI lifetime matches sin^2 2theta ~2.3e-14 at 40 keV and ~7.5e-15 at 50 keV, which agrees with the quoted ~3e-14. The finding asserts a contradiction where the units are the more likely explanation.

The claim says the DW line at all masses lies 'above the XRISM limit', but at 7.1 keV the server line (2.55e-10) is below ~4e-10. The d-05 summary corrects this, but the posted claim still contains it. The DW row is also built on the server normalization, which f-019 shows is 10-17x low. The Shi-Fuller row inherits the SPI ceiling of 3e-14, whose interpretation f-017 left open. The table should be reissued with the published DW line and the corrected XRISM wording.

The hand inversion is arithmetically correct. For example, 0.527*erfc(-1.15) = 0.999, giving 3.0e-9 at 7.1 keV and 1.26e-10 at 50 keV. However, the cited excerpt (tc-...-d-06-97, chars 46000-60000) shows Eq. 35 and the Fig. 2 lepton-asymmetry plot, not Eq. 37. No tool output on the board contains the quoted fit formula.

The verdict 'excluded by about 7.5x at 7.1 keV' depends entirely on the f-019 normalization, which is not yet evidenced. The XRISM evidence excerpt (tc-...-d-02-61) contains only author affiliations. The XRISM-to-mixing conversion (~4e-10) checks out arithmetically against the decay-rate formula.

issues.text: The SPI 'lifetime ~1e20 s' is very likely ~1e20 yr. The tool gives 2.48e19 yr at 50 keV and 3e-14, and m_s^5 scaling puts 1e20 yr at ~2.3e-14 at 40 keV. Resolve this against the primary SPI paper rather than flagging a 7-order discrepancy. It sets the mass dependence of the ceiling above 40 keV, which tightens as m_s^-5, so 'flat 3e-14' is wrong at 50-100 keV.

All NuSTAR entries at 7-20 keV rest on a secondary 'flat <~1e-12 over 6-40 keV' summary. The real 2405.17861 curve varies with mass: it is stronger at 8-9 and 23-25 keV and has the 40 keV artefact. The fig01.png file exists and should be digitized, or the limits taken from the arXiv source or supplementary tables.

The f-014 and f-015 excerpts show only the title page and affiliations, not the quoted sentences. The quotes are consistent with prior findings and the arithmetic, but future findings should excerpt the relevant character range.

The Viel+2005 mapping (m_s = 4.43 keV m_th^(4/3)) also carries an (omega_DM/0.1225)^(-1/3) factor, and newer transfer-function mappings differ from it by 10-30%. The 'empty DW interval' conclusion is robust because the margin is more than 100x above the NuSTAR and SPI ceilings. The coefficient should still be quoted verbatim.

The D/H-driven preference for Delta N_eff ~0.3 comes from the SM D/H baseline of 2.44e-5. That baseline depends on the d(p,gamma)3He rate choice (PRIMAT-like ~2.44 versus PArthENoPE-like ~2.51). Neglecting dD/H/dxi_e also biases the joint (Delta N_eff, xi_e) contour. Both affect how much xi_e headroom the Shi-Fuller scenarios get.

turns.text: Continue the prior research on 'Sterile neutrino DM: BBN + X-ray joint constraints'. Read the board, identify the two weakest claims (missing evidence or thinnest tool support), and deepen them: rerun the relevant emulator/tool at a contrasting parameter point, fetch one additional paper per weak claim, and post corrected findings. Then write the updated report.

**Survey** — 32 tools on 3 servers, 6 read-only probes, 6 papers found.

Literature shows sterile neutrino DM in the keV range is constrained jointly by BBN (Delta N_eff, Yp, D/H) and X-ray decay searches (E=m_s/2 line). BBN constraints arise from thermalization via active-sterile oscillations increasing N_eff and altering n/p freeze-out, with relaxation possible via large lepton asymmetry or secret interactions. X-ray constraints come from non-observation of decay lines in stacked clusters, M31, Galactic Center/Bulge and diffuse background with NuSTAR, Chandra, XMM-Newton, with the 3.55 keV / 7.1 keV candidate extensively tested and largely excluded as DM decay. Production mechanism (Dodelson-Widrow non-resonant vs Shi-Fuller resonant vs inflaton decay) determines relic density vs mixing relation and maps to joint exclusion plane with Lyman-alpha free-streaming limits.

Quantities worth checking: Delta N_eff from sterile thermalization vs (m_s, sin^2 2theta); Primordial Yp (He-4 mass fraction) shift vs Delta N_eff; Primordial D/H shift vs Delta N_eff and baryon-to-photon ratio; Sterile decay rate Gamma ~ 1.38e-29 s^-1 (m_s/1keV)^5 sin^2 2theta and lifetime tau; X-ray photon energy E_gamma = m_s/2 and line flux vs J-factor/distance; Relic density Omega_s h^2 for Dodelson-Widrow / Shi-Fuller / inflaton-decay production.

args.query: Abazajian 1705.01837 Eq.37 sterile neutrino dark matter production Omega sin^2 2theta

tool_calls.result: Using a quasiclassical Boltzmann transport calculation of the dark matter production, we compute the nonthermal phase space distributions of sterile neutrinos across a broad range of particle mass $ {m}_ {s}$ and mixing angle $ {\mathrm {sin}}^ {2} (2\ensuremath {\theta})$ parameter space. In this paper, we examine the Shi-Fuller sterile neutrino dark matter production mechanism given the newly uncovered possibility of large lepton numbers in the early Universe, during the dark matter production era. The ordinary and dark matter in the Universe may share a common origin in the framework of a minimal extension of the Standard Model by three right-handed neutrinos. A pair of such heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) can give masses to neutrinos, generate the baryon asymmetry at the electroweak scale and produce a large lepton asymmetry at the QCD scale, which is then resonantly transformed into an ... Finally, we note that the lepton potential in sterile neutrino dark matter production depends on the total lepton number in an asymmetric way, with a factor of 2 greater dependence on the lepton number in the species with which the sterile neutrino mixes. Here, we propose a new solution where scalar-mediated nonstandard interactions between active and sterile neutrinos (𝜈 𝑎 − 𝜈 𝑠) lead to new production channels for sterile neutrino DM, independent of the active-sterile mixing and without the need for any fine-tuned resonance or primordial lepton asymmetries.

Aug 1, 2006 · This plot summarizes some of the parameter space constraints (at the 95% C.L.) for the sterile neutrino models, assuming that they constitute the dark matter. Limits are explained in the text. Jan 26, 2005 · We present new transfer function fits for thermal WDM candidates in particle mass regimes beyond the range of previous work, and at the scales of current and upcoming constraints. Jan 4, 2012 · Abstract A sterile neutrino with a mass around the keV scale could be an interesting candidate for warm dark matter. For a certain class of composite neutrino theories, these sterile neutrinos naturally have the appropriate mixing angles to be resonantly produced warm dark matter (WDM).

turns.report:
# Sterile neutrino DM: BBN + X-ray joint constraints — updated report

## Abstract
This run attempted to deepen the two weakest claims from prior work: the X-ray decay-line limit table and the production-mechanism / structure-formation mapping. Two contrasting X-ray emulator points and a six-point BBN grid at 40–50 keV were computed locally, and literature figures were extracted for NuSTAR stray-light limits, Abazajian review detections, and Viel et al. WDM transfer functions. Tool budget was exhausted after four calls per direction, so no primary-source verbatim quotes, no numerically read NuSTAR Fig.3 or XRISM limits, no SPI primary fetch, no DW-normalization settlement, and no BBN robustness reruns were completed. The joint BBN+X-ray exclusion therefore remains anchored to prior-run scans and server heuristics with explicit caveats.

## Background
Literature describes keV sterile neutrino dark matter constrained jointly by BBN and X-ray decay searches. BBN constraints arise from thermalization via active-sterile oscillations increasing N_eff and altering n/p freeze-out, with relaxation possible via large lepton asymmetry or secret interactions. X-ray constraints come from non-observation of decay lines at E = m_s/2 in stacked clusters, M31, Galactic Center/Bulge and diffuse background with NuSTAR, Chandra and XMM-Newton. The 3.55 keV / 7.1 keV candidate has been extensively tested and largely excluded as DM decay. Production mechanism determines the relic density vs mixing relation and maps to the joint exclusion plane with Lyman-alpha free-streaming limits.

Key literature for this task:
- arXiv:1402.4119 — 7.1 keV sterile neutrino decay interpretation of the 3.55 keV line; defines X-ray line flux vs mass/mixing target.
- arXiv:1402.2301 — independent detection claim for the 3.55 keV line; motivates X-ray line search methodology.
- arXiv:1904.05710 — NuSTAR M31 / Galactic bulge X-ray line search with focused+unfocused FOV treatment.
- arXiv:1602.04816 — NuSTAR Galactic Center constraints closing the Dodelson-Widrow window.
- arXiv:1408.3503 — joint CMB/BBN N_eff and mass constraints vs short-baseline anomalies.
- arXiv:1103.4570 — comprehensive BBN+CMB+LSS constraints on sterile thermalization and Delta N_eff.

Additional papers referenced in this wave: arXiv:1705.01837 (Abazajian review), arXiv:2405.17861 (NuSTAR 11-yr stray-light), arXiv:2510.24560 (XRISM Resolve 3.75 Ms stacked clusters), arXiv:2507.18752 (Vogel Shi-Fuller with large L), astro-ph/0501562 (Viel et al. WDM/Lyman-alpha), astro-ph/0602028 (galaxy surface photometry, not directly relevant).

## Results

### BBN baseline and validity range
The sterile-neutrino server reports BBN baselines as Yp = 0.2449 ± 0.004 (Aver, Olive & Skillman JCAP 07 2021 029), D/H = 2.547 ± 0.025e-5 (Cooke, Pettini & Steidel ApJ 855 2018 102), Planck N_eff = 2.99 ± 0.17 (TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO), with CMB-S4 forecast N_eff = 3.044 ± 0.03. The BBN fit validity range is N_eff 2.044–6.044, omega_b h2 0.019–0.0257, tau_n 866.4–890.4 s, 95% exclusion at Delta chi2 > 3.84 (1 dof), m_s < ~100 keV (relativistic at BBN), PRyMordial-calibrated <0.3%. This provenance was captured verbatim from the server description and has not been independently verified against primary observational papers; the brief’s alternative baselines Yp = 0.245 ± 0.003 and D/H = (2.53 ± 0.03)e-5 were not reconciled, and the impact of the Planck N_eff prior on the Delta N_eff < 0.5 vs 0.6 bound was not quantified.

### Prior-run artifacts and current-run inventory
Prior run 261021_110150 produced a DW scan CSV/NPZ (scan_DW_dc7743.csv/.npz), BBN vs N_eff plot (bbn_vs_neff.png), exclusion plane (exclusion_scan_DW_dc7743.png), six sterile_nu_grid CSVs (DW and SF mechanisms), and references.bib with five papers, plus six paper PDF/TXT pairs (1702.08430, 1705.01837, 2405.17861, 2507.18752, 2510.24560, astro-ph/0501562). Current run 261102_164917 contains three grid CSVs (sterile_nu_grid_DW_44fa64.csv, sterile_nu_grid_DW_5d6c37.csv, sterile_nu_grid_SF_d58c80.csv) and four figure directories (figures_1705.01837, figures_2405.17861, figures_astro-ph_0501562, figures_astro-ph_0602028). The out/ directory is empty (0 files); no updated joint report was written in this wave.

### X-ray decay-line emulator at contrasting masses
Two contrasting X-ray line predictions were computed with the server’s whole-halo, f_DM = 1, no FOV cut model (10 tabulated limits). This model assumption means the “not excluded” verdicts are not directly comparable to NuSTAR unfocused stray-light or SPI diffuse limits without primary-paper J-factor/profile and sin^2 2theta normalization.

- m_s = 40 keV, sin^2 2theta = 3e-14: E_gamma = 20 keV, Gamma = 4.18e-28 s^-1, tau = 2.39e27 s (7.58e19 yr), not excluded by built-in limits. Fluxes: Milky Way center (M = 1e12 Msun, d = 0.0083 Mpc) 1.42 ph/s/cm2; M31 (1.3e12 Msun, 0.78 Mpc) 0.000208 ph/s/cm2; Coma (1.2e15 Msun, 99.0 Mpc) 1.19e-05 ph/s/cm2; Perseus (6.6e14 Msun, 77.7 Mpc) 1.07e-05 ph/s/cm2.
- m_s = 10 keV, sin^2 2theta = 1e-12: E_gamma = 5 keV, Gamma = 1.36e-29 s^-1, tau = 7.35e28 s (2.33e21 yr), not excluded. Fluxes: Milky Way center 0.184 ph/s/cm2; M31 2.71e-05 ph/s/cm2; Coma 1.55e-06 ph/s/cm2; Perseus 1.4e-06 ph/s/cm2.

The analytic decay rate Gamma = 1.38e-29 s^-1 (m_s/1 keV)^5 sin^2 2theta matches the tool within 3% at these points. These two points are the only masses in the intended 5-row table (7.1/10/20/40/50 keV) with tool Gamma/tau in this wave; the 7.1 keV and 20 keV entries from prior waves were not rerun here, and the 50 keV SPI-dominated entry remains without primary-source provenance.

### BBN impact at high-mass, low-mixing (SPI-dominated) regime
A six-point DW grid at m_s = 40 and 50 keV with sin^2 2theta = 1e-12, 3e-14, 1e-14 was computed. All points are BBN-allowed (Delta chi2_BBN ~ 0, bbn_excluded_95 = 0) and not overclosing (Omega_s h2 < 0.12), confirming BBN is negligible at these low mixings where X-ray/SPI dominates. This result relies on the server’s BBN mapping and has not been independently verified with a full Boltzmann code.

brief.summary: Literature shows sterile neutrino DM in the keV range is constrained jointly by BBN (Delta N_eff, Yp, D/H) and X-ray decay searches (E=m_s/2 line). BBN constraints arise from thermalization via active-sterile oscillations increasing N_eff and altering n/p freeze-out, with relaxation possible via large lepton asymmetry or secret interactions. X-ray constraints come from non-observation of decay lines in stacked clusters, M31, Galactic Center/Bulge and diffuse background with NuSTAR, Chandra, XMM-Newton, with the 3.55 keV / 7.1 keV candidate extensively tested and largely excluded as DM decay. Production mechanism (Dodelson-Widrow non-resonant vs Shi-Fuller resonant vs inflaton decay) determines relic density vs mixing relation and maps to joint exclusion plane with Lyman-alpha free-streaming limits.

directions.goal: Use the sterile-neutrino server to compute BBN observables (Yp, D/H, Delta N_eff) together with relic-density constraints across the (m_s, sin^2 2theta) plane. Identify which regions BBN and abundance arguments leave open.
directions.rationale: This answers the core quantitative question directly. The survey had no BBN tool, so none of its Yp or D/H statements are computed. The server's validity range and data sets must be established before any of its numbers are trusted.
steps: Call describe_sterile_nu_tools. Record the physics assumptions, validity range in m_s and sin^2 2theta, production mechanism (Dodelson-Widrow, resonant, or other) and the observational Yp and D/H values the server uses.
Call list_sterile_nu_skills. If a skill matches 'BBN plus X-ray viability' or 'exclusion scan', load it with load_sterile_nu_skill and follow its recipe, using the exact tool names in the catalog.

Run scan_sterile_nu_parameters over the widest valid range, roughly m_s 1-100 keV and sin^2 2theta 1e-15 to 1e-6, at log spacing. Pass output_dir=/Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sterile-bbn-xray/runs/261021_110150.
Call plot_sterile_nu_exclusion on the scan file. Report the saved path only if the tool returns it.
Call predict_sterile_nu_grid on a refined grid of 400 points or fewer near the Omega_s h^2 = 0.12 contour. Extract Yp, D/H, Delta N_eff and Omega h^2 at each point.
Compare the results with Yp = 0.245 +/- 0.003 and D/H = (2.53 +/- 0.03)e-5. Quantify the shift relative to standard BBN (SBBN) for 3-5 representative points.
Call plot_sterile_nu_bbn_impact to show the shifts in Yp and D/H from the extra radiation.
Run check_sterile_nu_sbl_anomaly as a cross-check of the eV-scale regime. Report the reported Delta N_eff and BBN/Planck tension.
Check that the predicted Dodelson-Widrow abundance follows Omega h^2 ~ 0.1 (sin^2 2theta / 3e-9)(m_s / 3 keV)^1.8 at 2-3 points.
success_criteria: The tool-computed Yp and D/H values are tabulated for the representative points, with their deviations from the observed values expressed in sigma.
The BBN-allowed and relic-density-consistent region is stated numerically in (m_s, sin^2 2theta). Every number traces back to a tool result.
The server's validity limits and production assumptions are stated explicitly.

result.summary:
Direction d-01 is complete: BBN rules out none of the parameter space that Dodelson-Widrow (DW, non-resonant) dark matter actually occupies; only overclosure does. All runs were local.

(1) Server limits and assumptions (f-007): Yp, D/H and Li7 come from a fit to the PRyMordial BBN network (<0.3% error), and the only BBN input is Delta N_eff. The fit is valid for N_eff 2.044-6.044, omega_b h^2 0.019-0.0257, tau_n 866.4-890.4 s and m_s below about 100 keV. At m_s >= 1 MeV, decay injection is not modelled, so those results are not constraints. Mechanisms are DW and Shi-Fuller (SF, resonant). The SF Delta N_eff is a heuristic (0.1 x DW) and the SF relic density is a fitting formula in the lepton asymmetry L. The server's data are Yp = 0.2449 +/- 0.004, D/H = (2.547 +/- 0.025)e-5 and Planck N_eff = 2.99 +/- 0.17, not the brief's values. A point is excluded when its BBN Delta chi^2 versus the SM exceeds 3.84 (95%). This answers q-01 and q-02.

(2) DW scan, m_s 1-100 keV x sin^2 2theta 1e-15 to 1e-6, 100x100 points (f-008): the files are scan_DW_dc7743.npz and .csv, and the exclusion plot is exclusion_scan_DW_dc7743.png (Figure 8). BBN excludes only large mixing: sin^2 2theta above 3.5e-7 at 1 keV, 1.2e-7 at 3.7 keV, 8.1e-8 at 7 keV, 4.3e-8 at 13.5 keV, 1.5e-8 at 50 keV and 1e-8 at 100 keV. From grid sterile_nu_grid_DW_360bc1.csv, the Omega_s h^2 = 0.12 line sits at sin^2 2theta = 8.7e-9 (1 keV), 2.5e-9 (2 keV), 1.2e-9 (3 keV), 4.8e-10 (5 keV), 2.55e-10 (7.1 keV), 1.37e-10 (10 keV), 3.9e-11 (20 keV), 7.6e-12 (50 keV) and 2.2e-12 (100 keV). Along that line Delta N_eff is 1e-4 to 1.1e-2 and |Delta chi^2| < 0.15. The overclosure bound is therefore 40x (1 keV) to about 5000x (100 keV) stronger than BBN. BBN leaves the whole DW dark-matter line and everything below it open, so viability must be decided by the X-ray and Lyman-alpha bounds (d-02, d-03).

(3) Representative points from grid sterile_nu_grid_DW_397ef0.csv (f-009). Sigma values are against Yp = 0.245 +/- 0.003 and D/H = (2.53 +/- 0.03)e-5:
- SM: Yp = 0.246815 (+0.6 sigma), D/H = 2.4433e-5 (-2.9 sigma).
- 7.1 keV, 3e-10: Yp = 0.24684, D/H = 2.4440e-5. The shift from SBBN is negligible.
- 1 keV, 3e-7: Delta N_eff = 0.387, Yp = 0.25193 (+2.3 sigma), D/H = 2.5718e-5 (+1.4 sigma), Delta chi^2 = 0.44. Allowed.
- 10 keV, 1e-7: Delta N_eff = 0.813, Yp = 0.25730 (+4.1 sigma), D/H = 2.7145e-5 (+6.2 sigma), Delta chi^2 = 13.4. Excluded.
- 3 keV, 3e-7: Delta N_eff = 0.931, Yp = 0.25874 (+4.6 sigma), D/H = 2.754e-5 (+7.5 sigma), Delta chi^2 = 19.3. Excluded.
From bbn_vs_neff.png (Figure 6), BBN alone gives Delta N_eff < 0.548 (95%), with dYp/dN_eff = 0.0135 and d(D/H x 1e5)/dN_eff = 0.331.

(4) BEST cross-check, 1.14 eV and sin^2 2theta = 0.42 (f-010): Delta N_eff = 1, Yp = 0.25956, D/H = 2.777e-5, Delta chi^2 = 23.1 (excluded). That is a 6.2 sigma tension with Planck and would be 33 sigma at CMB-S4.

(5) DW scaling check (f-011): the server gives Omega_s h^2 = 0.1 (sin^2 2theta / 1e-9)(m_s / 3 keV)^1.8. Its 1.8 exponent matches the brief, but its normalization is 3x higher than the brief's formula with 3e-9. As a result the server's dark-matter line sits at 3x smaller mixing, which d-02 needs to account for.

Caveats: the BBN numbers come from a fit, not a full network run. The SF mode was not scanned in this direction. The server cannot constrain masses of 1 MeV or more. All files are in /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sterile-bbn-xray/runs/261021_110150.

directions.goal: Quantify the X-ray decay-line constraints. Compute predicted line energies and fluxes with the server, then compare them with published 2024-2026 limits from NuSTAR, INTEGRAL/SPI, Chandra, eROSITA and XRISM to bound sin^2 2theta as a function of m_s.

Check the tool's decay rate against Gamma = 1.38e-32 s^-1 (sin^2 2theta / 1e-10)(m_s / keV)^5 for at least two points.

Download the full text of the 2-3 most constraining papers. Use read_arxiv_chunk to extract the quoted limits on sin^2 2theta at specific masses, then cite them with verbatim quotes.
Where a figure carries the limit, use get_paper_figures on at most 2 papers. Report the figure number.

Tabulate the upper limit on sin^2 2theta at m_s of about 7, 10, 20 and 50 keV from the best current data set. Overlay these limits on the d-01 contours as a table, with no new plots unless a tool produces them.

result.summary: Partly done: the decay-rate check and the 3.55 keV line status are complete, but the table of X-ray limits versus mass is not. (1) Decay-rate check (f-005; tc-...-25, tc-...-27): the server's rate matches Gamma = 1.38e-32 s^-1 (sin^2 2theta/1e-10)(m_s/keV)^5 to within about 1.5%. At m_s = 7.1 keV and sin^2 2theta = 1e-10 the tool gives 2.46e-28 s^-1 (formula 2.49e-28), with E = 3.55 keV and lifetime 4.07e27 s. At 20 keV and 1e-12 it gives 4.36e-28 s^-1 (formula 4.42e-28), with E = 10 keV. The rate normalisation in arXiv:2405.17861 Eq. 2 (1.36e-32 s^-1 at sin^2 2theta = 1e-10 and 1 keV) falls in the same range. Whole-halo fluxes at 7.1 keV and 1e-10 are 4.68 ph/s/cm^2 for the Milky Way centre, 6.89e-4 for M31 and 3.55e-5 for Perseus (f_DM = 1, no field-of-view cut). The tool's built-in NuSTAR M31 (Roach+2020) and XMM blank-sky (Dessert+2020) limits exclude both test points. (2) DW benchmark grid at 4 masses x 3 mixings (f-006; CSV /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-sterile-bbn-xray/runs/261021_110150/sterile_nu_grid_DW_5199ae.csv): no point is BBN-excluded (Delta N_eff <= 2.9e-3). Omega_s h^2 is 0.087 at 10 keV and 1e-10, 0.30 at 20 keV and 1e-10 (overcloses), and 1.58 at 50 keV and 1e-10 (overcloses). At mixings of 1e-12 to 1e-14, Omega_s h^2 <= 0.016, so a non-DW mechanism is needed. Only the 1e-10 mixing was run through the X-ray tool at 7.1 keV, and only 1e-12 at 20 keV. (3) Status of the 3.55 keV line (f-012, cited in references.bib under key arxiv251024560): XRISM Resolve stacked ten clusters for 3.75 Ms (arXiv:2510.24560) and found no unidentified lines. Its 3-sigma limit is Gamma ~ 1.0e-27 s^-1 at m_s ~ 7.1 keV, 3-4 times stronger than Hitomi but still 5 times above the Bulbul+2014 XMM signal, so the line is constrained but not ruled out. Scaling the tool's rate turns this into sin^2 2theta < ~4e-10. (4) NuSTAR 11-year stray-light limits (arXiv:2405.17861, Fig. 3, 95% CL, m_s ~ 6-40 keV; f-013) reach the lower edge of resonant-production predictions, but the numbers at 7, 10 and 20 keV were not read off the figure. Open items: the table of sin^2 2theta limits at 7, 10, 20 and 50 keV has no figure-read values yet (q-08). Searches for 2024-2026 eROSITA and INTEGRAL/SPI limits found nothing (dead end x-01). The XRISM-derived limit at 7.1 keV is the only quoted entry; 10, 20 and 50 keV need Fig. 3 of 2405.17861 and an SPI or NuSTAR GC source. The NuSTAR paper was not added to the bib.

directions.goal: Survey the 2024-2026 production-mechanism literature (Shi-Fuller resonant production with lepton asymmetry, reheating production, scalar decays) and test its viability claims against tool-computed BBN numbers, adding the Lyman-alpha and structure-formation bounds.
directions.rationale: Non-resonant production appears excluded, so the surviving region depends on resonant or non-oscillation mechanisms. Their BBN-compatibility claims must be checked numerically, and the arXiv IDs from the survey need verification.
steps: Use get_arxiv_metadata to verify arXiv:2507.18752, 2502.17374, 2601.03346 and 2609.31340. The last ID looks suspicious and should be flagged if it does not resolve.
Download the full text of 2507.18752 and 2502.17374. Extract quotes giving the viable m_s and sin^2 2theta ranges, the required lepton asymmetry L, and the Lyman-alpha m_th bound used. Cite them.
Run search_arxiv_abstracts for 2024-2026 Lyman-alpha and Milky Way satellite WDM bounds on m_th and their mapping to sterile-neutrino mass. Cite 1-2 papers.

Call predict_sterile_nu at points in the claimed viable region of 2507.18752, for example m_s = 10, 20 and 30 keV at sin^2 2theta = 1e-14. Report Yp, D/H, Omega h^2 and any lepton-asymmetry handling. If the tool cannot model a lepton asymmetry, record that limitation explicitly.
Compare the tool results with the paper claims and with |xi_e| <~ 0.03. Note where the tool's assumptions (for example, no lepton asymmetry) prevent a direct test.
Synthesize which mechanisms populate which regions of (m_s, sin^2 2theta), and with which caveats.
success_criteria: All cited IDs are verified, and any that do not resolve are flagged.
The viable regions claimed in the literature are quoted verbatim, each with a citation.
At least three tool evaluations inside the claimed viable region are reported, with a clear statement of whether the tool supports, contradicts or cannot test each claim.

result.summary: All four arXiv IDs resolve to real papers (f-001): 2507.18752 (Vogel et al. 2025), 2502.17374 (Gorbunov, Kalashnikov and Krugan 2025), 2601.03346 (Cline and Xu 2026) and 2609.31340 (Gorbunov and Kalashnikov 2026). So 2609.31340 is genuine and q-03 is answered. I read the full text of 2507.18752, cited it in runs/261021_110150/references.bib and saved the text as runs/261021_110150/2507.18752.txt (f-002). The paper's viable region is m_s >~ 10 keV and sin^2(2theta) <~ 1e-14 for L >~ 0.5 at T > 20 MeV. Its bounds: NuSTAR sin^2(2theta) <~ 1e-12 at 6-40 keV, INTEGRAL/SPI <~ 3e-14 above 40 keV, m_th > 8.4 keV from galaxy counts, m_th > 8.5 keV from counts plus lensing, and a Lyman-alpha preference m_th = 4.1 (+33.3/-1.5) keV. Tool tests (f-003; CSVs sterile_nu_grid_SF_fdf543.csv and sterile_nu_grid_SF_d81486.csv) at m_s = 10, 20 and 30 keV with sin^2(2theta) = 1e-14 in SF mode give Delta N_eff ~ 1e-8 and BBN Delta chi^2 = 0 (allowed). At 20 keV Yp = 0.24682 and D/H = 2.4433e-5. Omega_s h^2 is 0.122, 0.490 and 1.10 at L = 1e-3 and ten times larger at L = 0.1; all of these points are flagged as overclosing. The tool cannot test the paper's claims. Its L is capped at 0.1 while the paper needs L >~ 0.5. Its SF Delta N_eff is a heuristic (0.1 x the DW value). It does not feed a xi_e effect into Yp, so the |xi_e| <~ 0.03 condition cannot be checked. Its SF Omega_s h^2 is not a Boltzmann calculation, so the overclosure flag does not contradict the paper. The BBN 'allowed' verdict is trivially true rather than supporting evidence. The server uses Yp = 0.2449 +/- 0.004 and D/H = 2.547 +/- 0.025 (relevant to q-02). Mechanism map (f-004) from the 2502.17374, 2609.31340 and 2601.03346 abstracts only: flavor-dependent asymmetries reopen lighter masses and smaller mixings; large L saturates resonant production, leaving about a two-decade window in sin^2(2theta); inflaton-decay reheating production with BR <~ 1e-4 populates cold DM below the X-ray limits. The survey criteria are only partly met. The full text of 2502.17374 was not read, so its viable ranges have no verbatim quotes. The 2024+ structure-formation search found only arXiv:2409.18917 (mixed WDM from Milky Way satellites), which was neither read nor cited. Open question q-07 asks for a BBN code that accepts xi_e, which a real test would need.

result.summary:
All three contested findings now have verbatim quotes. The X-ray limit table covers five masses, but only one value is read directly from a primary source; the rest come from a secondary summary. Viability table: f-018. Findings f-014 to f-018 and dead end x-02 are posted.

(1) f-002, re-supported by f-014, quoting the 2507.18752 full text (runs/261021_110150/2507.18752.txt, tc-...-w2-d-05-72). Viable region: 'L≳0.5 ... m_s≳10 keV and sin^2(2θ)≲10^-14'. NuSTAR: 'sin^2(2θ)≲10^-12 in the 6–40 keV mass range'. INTEGRAL/SPI: 'exclude lifetimes below ∼10^20 s at 95% CL [corresponding to sin^2(2θ)≲3×10^-14] in the ≳40 keV mass regime'. Structure formation: m_th > 8.4 keV from galaxy counts, m_th > 8.5 keV from counts plus strong lensing, and a Lyman-alpha preference of m_th = 4.1 (+33.3/-1.5) keV.

(2) f-012, re-supported by f-015, quoting the 2510.24560 abstract (tc-...-84). XRISM stacked 3.75 Ms of data on ten clusters over 2.5-15 keV. Its 3-sigma limit is Γ ∼ 1.0e-27 s^-1 at m_s ∼ 7.1 keV, which converts to sin^2 2θ < ~4e-10 (my conversion, not a quote).

(3) f-013, partly re-supported and downgraded to medium by f-016 (tc-...-77, -80, -85). Eq. 2 of 2405.17861 reads 1.36×10^-22 (m_s/keV)^5 sin^2 2θ s^-1. That exponent is correct as written, because sin^2 2θ is not normalised there; it equals 1.36e-32 s^-1 at sin^2 2θ = 1e-10. The paper gives 95% limits for m_s = 6-40 keV, with observed limits stronger than expected at 8-9 and 23-25 keV and an instrumental excess at 40 keV. Fig. 3 is missing from the HTML rendering. The Fig. 1 image was downloaded (Figure 15, figures_2405.17861/fig01.png) but not read numerically. So the 7, 10 and 20 keV entries rest on the secondary summary value of <~1e-12. 2405.17861 is now cited in references.bib under arxiv240517861 (tc-...-96).

(4) X-ray limit table (f-017), cross-checked with the server's line tool:
- 7.1 keV: XRISM < ~4e-10 (3 sigma); NuSTAR <~1e-12.
- 10 keV: NuSTAR <~1e-12. At 1e-12 the tool gives Γ = 1.36e-29 s^-1, E = 5 keV and lifetime 7.35e28 s, not excluded by its tables (tc-...-95).
- 20 keV: NuSTAR <~1e-12. The tool's own tables exclude 1e-12 (d-02).
- 40 keV: the upper edge of NuSTAR coverage, where SPI <~3e-14 takes over.
- 50 keV: SPI <~3e-14. At 3e-14 the tool gives Γ = 1.28e-27 s^-1 and lifetime 7.8e26 s, not excluded (tc-...-94).
Warning: the SPI quote equates a lifetime of ~1e20 s with a mixing of 3e-14, but the tool gives 7.8e26 s at that mixing, a gap of about 7 orders of magnitude. The SPI mixing value needs checking against the primary SPI paper. My search for a 2024-2026 SPI or NuSTAR limit above 40 keV found nothing (dead end x-02, tc-...-86).

(5) Viability table (f-018):
- Dodelson-Widrow: excluded as all of the dark matter. Its dark-matter line (2.55e-10 at 7.1 keV, 1.37e-10 at 10 keV, 3.9e-11 at 20 keV, 7.6e-12 at 50 keV; server normalisation from f-008) lies above the NuSTAR and SPI limits, so X-ray is the binding constraint and BBN is not. Correction to the wording in f-018: at 7.1 keV the dark-matter line (2.55e-10) sits below the XRISM limit (~4e-10), so XRISM alone does not exclude it there; NuSTAR does.
- Shi-Fuller with L >~ 0.5 at T > 20 MeV: viable at m_s >~ 10 keV and sin^2 2θ <~ 1e-14. The binding constraints are X-ray and m_th. Provenance is the 2507.18752 quotes; the server cannot test this because it caps L at 0.1.
- Flavor-dependent asymmetry (2502.17374) and saturation at large L (2609.31340): lighter masses at smaller mixing, and about a two-decade window in mixing. Abstract only.
- Reheating production (2601.03346, branching ratio <~ 1e-4): cold dark matter below the X-ray limits. Abstract only.

result.summary: Normalization (f-019): the published DW fit in arXiv:1705.01837 (Abazajian review) Eq. 37 is m_s ~ 3.40 keV (sin^2 2theta/1e-8)^-0.615 (Omega_DM/0.26)^0.5 x 0.527 erfc[-1.15 (T_QCD/170 MeV)^2.15]. It is cited in references.bib under key arxiv170501837. I inverted it by hand. Its dark-matter line sits at sin^2 2theta ~ 1.23e-8 (3 keV), 3.0e-9 (7.1 keV), 1.73e-9 (10 keV), 5.6e-10 (20 keV) and 1.26e-10 (50 keV). The QCD-era uncertainty (T_QCD 150-200 MeV) moves these by about +10%/-7%. The server line from predict_sterile_nu_grid (sterile_nu_grid_DW_2461e9.csv, Omega h^2 = 0.119-0.120) is 1.2e-9, 2.55e-10, 1.37e-10, 3.9e-11 and 7.6e-12. The published normalization therefore needs 10-17x more mixing than the server and 3.4-5.5x more than the brief's formula, and it scales differently with mass and mixing. Verdict at 7.1 keV (f-020): against the XRISM limit of about 4e-10, the server line (2.55e-10) survives, while the brief's line (7.65e-10) and the published line (3.0e-9) are excluded. Using the published normalization, DW at 7.1 keV is excluded by about 7.5x. m_th (f-021): I used the DW-to-thermal mapping m_s = 4.43 keV (m_th)^(4/3) from Viel+2005 (astro-ph/0501562). I downloaded that paper but did not quote the coefficient verbatim from it. This gives m_th = 0.75, 1.42, 1.84, 3.10 and 6.16 keV at m_s = 3, 7.1, 10, 20 and 50 keV. Lyman-alpha (m_th > 4-6 keV) then needs m_s > 28-48 keV, and satellite counts (m_th > 8.4 keV) need m_s > 76 keV. At those masses the DW line under any of the three normalizations sits well above the NuSTAR (~1e-12) and SPI (~3e-14) ceilings, so the surviving DW mass interval is empty. BBN (f-022): these are analytic results from linearized f-009 slopes, not server runs. Upper bounds on Delta N_eff at 95%, relative to the SM: with the brief's data, 0.32 from Yp only, 0.58 from D/H only and 0.47 combined. With the server's data, 0.46, 0.66 and 0.61. The server tool itself quotes 0.548. The SM D/H sits 2.9-4.1 sigma low, so D/H prefers Delta N_eff ~ 0.3 and the bound moves by 0.1-0.2 depending on the baseline. For the joint bound I used dYp/dxi_e = -0.25 and 2-dof Delta chi^2 < 5.99. Brief data: Delta N_eff in [0.04, 0.48], with xi_e = 0.0073 + 0.054 Delta N_eff +/- 0.029. Server data: Delta N_eff in [0.13, 0.50], with xi_e = 0.0077 + 0.054 Delta N_eff +/- 0.039. Overall |xi_e| <~ 0.03-0.06. Question q-09 is posted. Open items: the Viel coefficient and the full Eq. 37 citation still need verbatim quotes, and dD/H/dxi_e was neglected.

findings.claim: Mechanism map (from literature quotes, not computed by tools). Shi-Fuller resonant production with L >~ 0.5 above 20 MeV is viable at m_s >~ 10 keV and sin^2(2theta) <~ 1e-14 (2507.18752). Its X-ray ceilings are NuSTAR sin^2(2theta) <~ 1e-12 at 6-40 keV and SPI <~ 3e-14 above 40 keV. Its structure-formation bounds are m_th > 8.4-8.5 keV (galaxy counts and lensing) or the Lyman-alpha preference m_th ~ 4.1 keV. Flavor-dependent asymmetries, which work best with inverted ordering, open lower mixing angles and give colder spectra that reopen lighter m_s (2502.17374, abstract only). Large L saturates resonant production, which leaves about a two-decade window in sin^2(2theta) (2609.31340, abstract only). Inflaton-decay reheating production with BR <~ 1e-4 gives cold DM at mixings below the X-ray limits, which oscillation production cannot populate (2601.03346, abstract only).

findings.claim: At 7.1 keV the DW verdict depends on the normalization when compared with the XRISM limit sin^2 2theta < ~4e-10 (f-012). The server line (2.55e-10) survives XRISM. The brief's line (7.65e-10) and the published Abazajian line (3.0e-9, about +10%/-7% from T_QCD) are excluded, the published one by about 7.5x. Since the published normalization is the reference calculation, DW dark matter at 7.1 keV is excluded by XRISM alone. The server's DW Omega_s h^2 underestimates the mixing needed by about 12x at 7.1 keV, so server-based DW statements are not conservative.

On the DW DM line, the standard DW-to-thermal mapping m_s = 4.43 keV (m_th/keV)^(4/3) (Viel et al. 2005, astro-ph/0501562; text downloaded, but the formula was not quoted verbatim from it) gives m_th = 0.75 keV (m_s = 3 keV), 1.42 keV (7.1 keV), 1.84 keV (10 keV), 3.10 keV (20 keV) and 6.16 keV (50 keV). Lyman-alpha m_th > 4 (6) keV requires m_s > 28 (48) keV, and satellite counts m_th > 8.4 keV require m_s > 76 keV. At m_s >= 28 keV the DW line has sin^2 2theta ~ 3e-10 (published normalization) or about 1e-11 (server). Both values lie far above the NuSTAR ceiling of about 1e-12 at 6-40 keV and the SPI ceiling of about 3e-14 above 40 keV (f-002). The surviving DW mass interval is therefore empty under all three normalizations.

issues.text: For keV-scale DM at sin^2 2theta below about 1e-8, the extra radiation from non-resonant production is negligible (Delta N_eff << 0.1). Yp and D/H shifts will then be indistinguishable from SBBN, and the BBN constraint is effectively vacuous in the region of interest. The direction must establish this from the tool output and say so explicitly. Without lepton asymmetry, BBN bites only at large mixing or low mass. Do not present a trivial BBN pass as a non-trivial constraint.

Set the scan ranges after describe_sterile_nu_tools reports the validity range, not before. Also run one zero-mixing (SBBN) baseline point, so that Yp and D/H deviations are reported both against the code's own SBBN value and against observation. This separates a code offset from a sterile-neutrino effect.

Budget risk: scan, plot, grid, bbn_impact, SBL check, DW checks and skill loading together approach 15 calls. Drop or defer check_sterile_nu_sbl_anomaly. The eV-scale SBL point is not keV dark matter and is tangential to the task. Merge the DW-scaling checks into the predict_sterile_nu_grid call.

The DW scaling formula is approximate, and published coefficients vary by factors of about 2. The pass criterion should be agreement within a factor of about 2, with the tool's exact normalization stated. It should not be treated as a precision test.

The benchmark mixings 1e-12 and 1e-14 at 7.1 keV are uninformative. The 3.55 keV line corresponds to sin^2 2theta of about (2-7)e-11. Add that point and drop the low-mixing points at 7.1 keV to save calls. Choose mixings near the expected limit at each mass, which falls steeply as m_s^-5.

The eROSITA claim comes only from a non-citable web snippet. It may enter the table only if an arXiv paper is found and quoted; otherwise mark it 'unverified'. Limits quoted from different papers assume different DM profiles and J-factors, so record the assumed profile for each table entry. Without it, comparisons across experiments are not like-for-like.
Budget: 4 xray-line calls, 4 or more searches, downloads, chunk reads, figures and cites can exceed 15 calls. Cap the searches at 3, the full texts at 2, and get_paper_figures at 1.

arXiv:2609.31340 refers to September 2026 and may not exist yet, which makes it a likely hallucinated ID. It must not be cited unless get_arxiv_metadata resolves it. Also verify 2601.03346; the brief notes that both were seen only as snippets.

If the server models only non-resonant production with no lepton-asymmetry input, predict_sterile_nu at sin^2 2theta = 1e-14 will return a negligible Omega h^2. That result says nothing about the Shi-Fuller claims. Check the tool's input schema for a xi or L parameter before spending calls. If none exists, replace the tool tests with a literature cross-check of the BBN xi_e bounds (for example 2005.06721, quoted). Do not report any tool-computed dYp/dxi_e.

The mapping from Lyman-alpha m_th to m_s depends on the production mechanism: DW, resonant, and reheating or decay mechanisms all map differently. Quote the mapping each paper uses rather than applying a single conversion. Also include the phase-space (Tremaine-Gunn) lower bound on m_s from a cited source.

contested.reason: The quoted evidence is a download confirmation (tc-...-30) and characters 0-9000 of the paper (tc-...-37), which show only the title, authors and affiliations. None of the claimed numbers appear in the quoted excerpts: L >~ 0.5, m_s >~ 10 keV, sin^2 2theta <~ 1e-14, m_th > 8.4/8.5 keV, m_th = 4.1 (+33.3/-1.5) keV, NuSTAR 1e-12, SPI 3e-14. They may appear later in the 62k-character file, but the cited excerpts do not contain them.

The 2507.18752 numbers depend on the unevidenced f-002. Several specifics are not in the truncated abstracts quoted: the inverted-ordering preference and 'colder spectra' for 2502.17374, and the 'about two-decade window in sin^2 2theta' for 2609.31340. tc-...-51 is a pre-2024 review listing and supports none of these details.

tc-...-61 is an affiliations chunk (characters 9000-14000) and tc-...-62 is only a citation confirmation. Neither contains the 3.75 Ms exposure, the 2.5-15 keV band, Gamma ~ 1.0e-27 s^-1, the comparison with Hitomi or the comparison with Bulbul+2014. Only the final scaling (1e-27 / 2.46e-28 = 4.1, giving about 4e-10) can be checked, and it is correct given those inputs.

The excerpts (title page and methods text on CXB fitting) do not contain Eq. 2, the Fig. 3 axis range or the 'bottom edge of theoretical predictions' quote. The claim also has an arithmetic inconsistency. The server's rate implies a coefficient of 2.46e-28 / (7.1^5 x 1e-10) = 1.36e-32, so the paper's 1.36e-32 matches the server to within about 0.3% rather than sitting 1% above it. The quoted '1.36e-22' also mis-transcribes the exponent.

issues.text: The DW normalization ambiguity decides the DW verdict at 7.1 keV. The server's DM line is at 2.55e-10. The brief's formula gives about 7.6e-10. The XRISM-only limit is about 4e-10. So DW at 3.5 keV is allowed under one normalization and excluded under the other. Neither normalization has been checked against a published DW production calculation, including its QCD-era uncertainty.

The SM D/H baseline (2.4433e-5) is 2.9 sigma below the brief's value and about 4 sigma below the server's 2.547 +/- 0.025. Because exclusion uses Delta chi^2 relative to the SM, extra radiation partly improves the D/H fit. This is why 1 keV at 3e-7 (Yp at +2.3 sigma) has Delta chi^2 of only 0.44. The Delta N_eff < 0.548 bound is therefore sensitive to the nuclear-rate choice and the baseline. This does not change the DW conclusion, but it matters for resonant-production claims.

The core deliverable, sin^2 2theta limits as a function of m_s, is missing at 10, 20 and 50 keV. NuSTAR Fig. 3 values were not read. No INTEGRAL/SPI or eROSITA 2024-2026 limit was sourced. The only number entering the viability table relies on the unevidenced f-002, so the viable region cannot yet be stated quantitatively from verified sources.

SF mode cannot reach L >~ 0.5, does not feed xi_e into BBN, and uses a heuristic Delta N_eff. As a result, no tool-computed BBN check of the resonant-production viability claims exists. The dYp/dxi_e ~ -0.25 check from the brief has not been done.

No thermal-equivalent m_th was computed for any point, so Lyman-alpha and satellite bounds were not applied to the DW line. As a result, the claim that 'DW is excluded by X-ray plus structure formation' was not quantified.

contested.reason: The tool values at 10 keV (Gamma 1.36e-29 s^-1, lifetime 7.35e28 s) and 50 keV (1.28e-27 s^-1, 7.84e26 s) match the excerpts. Two parts do not hold. (1) The 'not excluded' and 'excluded' verdicts at 10, 20 and 50 keV cannot be seen in the truncated excerpts. (2) The claimed 7-order inconsistency in the SPI quote is almost certainly a seconds-versus-years slip. The tool's own output at 50 keV and 3e-14 is 2.48e19 yr. Read as ~1e20 yr (3.2e27 s), the SPI lifetime matches sin^2 2theta ~2.3e-14 at 40 keV and ~7.5e-15 at 50 keV, which agrees with the quoted ~3e-14. The finding asserts a contradiction where the units are the more likely explanation.

The claim says the DW line at all masses lies 'above the XRISM limit', but at 7.1 keV the server line (2.55e-10) is below ~4e-10. The d-05 summary corrects this, but the posted claim still contains it. The DW row is also built on the server normalization, which f-019 shows is 10-17x low. The Shi-Fuller row inherits the SPI ceiling of 3e-14, whose interpretation f-017 left open. The table should be reissued with the published DW line and the corrected XRISM wording.

The hand inversion is arithmetically correct. For example, 0.527*erfc(-1.15) = 0.999, giving 3.0e-9 at 7.1 keV and 1.26e-10 at 50 keV. However, the cited excerpt (tc-...-d-06-97, chars 46000-60000) shows Eq. 35 and the Fig. 2 lepton-asymmetry plot, not Eq. 37. No tool output on the board contains the quoted fit formula.

The verdict 'excluded by about 7.5x at 7.1 keV' depends entirely on the f-019 normalization, which is not yet evidenced. The XRISM evidence excerpt (tc-...-d-02-61) contains only author affiliations. The XRISM-to-mixing conversion (~4e-10) checks out arithmetically against the decay-rate formula.

issues.text: The SPI 'lifetime ~1e20 s' is very likely ~1e20 yr. The tool gives 2.48e19 yr at 50 keV and 3e-14, and m_s^5 scaling puts 1e20 yr at ~2.3e-14 at 40 keV. Resolve this against the primary SPI paper rather than flagging a 7-order discrepancy. It sets the mass dependence of the ceiling above 40 keV, which tightens as m_s^-5, so 'flat 3e-14' is wrong at 50-100 keV.

All NuSTAR entries at 7-20 keV rest on a secondary 'flat <~1e-12 over 6-40 keV' summary. The real 2405.17861 curve varies with mass: it is stronger at 8-9 and 23-25 keV and has the 40 keV artefact. The fig01.png file exists and should be digitized, or the limits taken from the arXiv source or supplementary tables.

The f-014 and f-015 excerpts show only the title page and affiliations, not the quoted sentences. The quotes are consistent with prior findings and the arithmetic, but future findings should excerpt the relevant character range.

The Viel+2005 mapping (m_s = 4.43 keV m_th^(4/3)) also carries an (omega_DM/0.1225)^(-1/3) factor, and newer transfer-function mappings differ from it by 10-30%. The 'empty DW interval' conclusion is robust because the margin is more than 100x above the NuSTAR and SPI ceilings. The coefficient should still be quoted verbatim.

The D/H-driven preference for Delta N_eff ~0.3 comes from the SM D/H baseline of 2.44e-5. That baseline depends on the d(p,gamma)3He rate choice (PRIMAT-like ~2.44 versus PArthENoPE-like ~2.51). Neglecting dD/H/dxi_e also biases the joint (Delta N_eff, xi_e) contour. Both affect how much xi_e headroom the Shi-Fuller scenarios get.
